sources.document: TPS62901 data sheet, section 7.5.1 Layout Guidelines, page 41, figure 7-85
applied: Input capacitors adjacent to VIN/GND; short high-current loop and compact SW copper.
Inductors to the left of the RPJ9 package with their SW terminals facing pin 2.
VOS routed separately from SW to the actual local output-capacitor terminal.
MODE, SS/TR and VSET resistors/capacitors near the IC and return to its quiet local ground.
Use appropriate VIN/GND thermal copper and vias after stackup and assembly rules are selected.

sources.document: LTC2962/LTC2963/LTC2964 data sheet, Applications Information, page 17, figure 7
applied: Precision supervisors near the short board edge, away from switching inductors.
Separate low-resistance Kelvin branches for the measured rail and its load ground; reset/reference return current must not create a shared sense-ground voltage.
Mechanical/solder stress can shift the threshold and temperature coefficient; placement near an edge helps but does not qualify lifetime accuracy.
No stress-isolation slots proposed until mechanics and card guides are reviewed.

sources.document: Trion T20 Data Sheet, recommended operating conditions
applied: Core and I/O supervisor sense feed/return must refer to the powered FPGA load, not only the converter terminals; rail voltage limits are defined at device pins.

switching: U1.2 to L1.1 and U2.2 to L2.1 are short horizontal SW paths. Keep this copper small and keep precision sense/control routes out of its near field.
L1.2 to C2.1 and L2.2 to C5.1 are output paths. Separate Kelvin VOS connections U1.3/C2.1 and U2.3/C5.1 from the switch path.
C1.1/U1.6 and C4.1/U2.6 form the VIN legs; C1.2/U1.4 and C4.2/U2.4 are the matching short local power-return legs. Adjacent ground vias and a continuous reference plane are still required.

C2.2 and C5.2 also require low-inductance returns to their respective U1.4/U2.4 power ground through the local ground copper and continuous plane; the ten selected centerlines do not complete these output-current loops.
Route MODE/SS/VSET to quiet local converter ground, not through high-current capacitor or inductor returns.
precision: Use a dedicated measured-load rail branch for the top of each divider and a paired low-resistance load-ground return for each divider bottom and LTC ground/EP.
Keep the high-impedance divider midpoint connections short and separate from SW, reset-current and reference-output routes; do not place switching power-return current in the sense-ground branch.
C7/C8/C9 adjacent to each supervisor VCC/GND. Preserve a continuous ground plane; do not create disconnected analogue-ground islands.
The exact FPGA Kelvin pickoff pins and power-plane geometry must be chosen in the integrated PCB.
reset: U6 is at the right side of the local-power region to approach the FPGA reset logic. C10 adjacent to VCC and R108 adjacent to output.
MC_RAILS_OK_5V stays the 5V raw U5 reset signal. Only U6 output FPGA_CRESET_N is the qualified 3V3-domain copy.
The downstream reset AND input remains a separate integrated interface. No additional push-pull driver may connect directly to U6 output.

placement_screening.method: KiCad 10 native footprints: standard courtyard, or custom body/pads envelope inflated by 0.25mm; conservative axis-aligned envelope screening

limitations: Placement proposal only; native combined-board courtyard, mechanical and copper DRC must run after import.
Routing intent is not a complete routed board or physical timing proof.
Production layer stackup, copper weight, trace ampacity, thermal vias, solder rules and DC-bias-effective capacitance remain unqualified.
ADI solder-stress observation is not a guaranteed maximum; threshold/lifetime accuracy still requires mounted measurements.
Connector, guide, screw and FPGA load pickoff locations may require placement adjustment.
